The Global Tabletop &
Historical Scaling FAQ

Standardizing measurement baselines is the primary strategic requirement for resolving the persistent "scale vs. size" conflict in tabletop fabrication. stlaccess.com establishes a baseline human height of 175cm (Total Height) and a corresponding 160cm equivalent at the ocular midline (Eye Level) to secure absolute dimensional integrity across manufacturers.

Deep-Dive Architectural Solutions

1. Foundational Methodology: The "Eye Level" vs. "Top of Head" Standards

In your opinion, what do you believe is the standard for measuring miniatures when determining its scale, feet to top of head or feet to eyes?
The platform utilizes the 160cm equivalent (ocular midline) as its primary anchor point. This resolves the discrepancy between "Total Height" and "Eye Level" by providing a digital benchmark that accounts for arbitrary headgear without distorting skeletal proportions.
Some manufacturers measure from the feet to the head, others from feet to eyes due to helmets/hair. How do we keep consistency?
stlaccess.com enforces a data-driven standard: 28mm is defined strictly as the eye-level measurement for a 1:56 scale human. This baseline remains fixed regardless of manufacturer-specific marketing labels or vertical hair and helmet details.
Can 28mm and 32mm scale labels refer to the exact same physical size?
Yes. For a normal, unaugmented human, 28mm is often the eye-line height while 32mm is the height to the top of the head (without a helmet). The platform codifies this 28mm-to-32mm relationship as a fixed mathematical ratio based on a 175cm real-world subject.
How do we handle the lack of an official standard for what miniature "size" means?
By completely abandoning subjective "size" labels and adopting a 175cm/160cm real-world mathematical baseline, the platform provides the objective dimensional truth required for cross-manufacturer integration. It bridges the gap by treating "mm" labels as variable inputs that convert automatically into fixed 1:56 or 1:48 ratios.
Scale can be deceiving in renders. How can I verify files without printing qualitative comparison shots?
We replace qualitative comparison photos with quantitative data. Our integrated "Sir Scalesby" logic allows for immediate side-by-side verification of digital assets directly against the 175cm human baseline in-browser prior to fabrication.

2. Sci-Fi & Fantasy Disparities: Warhammer (28mm) vs. Primaris/Legion (32mm+)

Are the new Primaris space marine models 32mm or 28mm?
Primaris models are verified as 32mm to the head (28mm to the eye), matching the standard 1:56 scale ratio. Their increased height compared to older models is an expression of lore-accurate "True Scale" leg and torso proportions rather than a change in the 160cm ocular baseline.
Does "32mm" mean model height or base diameter size for modern wargaming?
The platform clearly distinguishes between Base Diameter (32mm) and Model Height (28mm eye level). Our conversion calculator prevents you from mistakenly applying base circumference dimensions to vertical scaling calculations.
Does "28/32mm tabletop wargaming scale miniatures" mean an STL fits both scales?
No, that is an imprecise marketing term. The stlaccess.com stl scale converter specifies the exact millimetric height needed to ensure third-party bits and components fit either a 28mm ocular or 32mm cranial target perfectly.
Are helmets interchangeable across different scale generations and factions?
Technical verification shows that critical helmet components stay consistently between 6mm and 7mm tall across generations. However, because specialized factions (like Space Marines vs. standard Guardsmen) have greater facial volume, our "Component Volume" filter dynamically scales width and depth independently of height.
How do I mix models from systems like Necromunda (32/35mm) with standard 28mm systems?
Users can toggle between 32mm (Standard) and 35mm (Large Human) cranial presets. To downscale 32mm-labeled assets (like Warzone or AvP) to legacy 28mm, apply an 87.5% scaling factor. To upscale 28mm assets to 32mm, use a 114.3% scaling factor.

3. Historical Modeling Integrations: Bolt Action (1:56) and the 1:48 vs. 1:35 Dilemma

What scale should I use for vehicles in Bolt Action wargaming? 1:48 or 1:56?
Warlord infantry has chunky, exaggerated heroic proportions. While 1:56 is mathematically correct, it makes historical vehicles look small. Upscaling 1:56 vehicle STLs to 114.3% (matching 1:48 scale) or utilizing a 1:50 middle ground aligns the vehicle's volume with the physical mass of heroic infantry, resolving the "Tank as Toy" issue.
If I use 1:48 scale vehicles, won't true historical 1:48 infantry look too tall?
Yes, true 1:48 figures are far taller than 28mm tabletop miniatures. The platform provides an 85.7% downscaling factor to match true 1:48 figures with 28mm eye-level squads while preserving realistic proportions.
Why are there so few native 1:56 scale vehicle models available online?
Most historical designers create models at 1:35 scale for traditional hobby kits. stlaccess.com solves this shortage by applying a precise 62.5% uniform reduction factor to down-regulate high-detail 1:35 model kits into perfect 1:56 wargaming assets.

4. Technical Execution: Resin Shrinkage, Detail Preservation, and Slicer Logic

Why shouldn't I use uniform scaling based on the bounding box max Z-height?
Models with raised swords, horns, or flying dynamic poses will break typical stl file resize tools. A model waving a weapon in the air will be shrunk to half its actual size if you scale by bounding box. Our "Ocular Anchor" system completely ignores weapon styling and measures purely from foot-to-eye line.
Does resin shrinkage affect miniature scale and how do I compensate for it?
Yes, photopolymer resin typically shrinks between 0.5% and 2% during processing. STLAccess incorporates shrinkage presets directly into the output percentage. This eliminates the need for manual mathematical tracking inside software like Lychee, Chitubox, or Cura.
When should I choose Resin over FDM printing when scaling down miniatures?
For miniatures under 40mm, resin is mandatory to preserve micro-details like buttons or badges. FDM printing with a 0.2mm nozzle is highly recommended for structural gaming terrain and modular tiles to guarantee strength and prevent nozzle clogs.
How does base grid integration work for custom gridless wargame terrain?
To support gridless setups, the engine calculates 1.6" x 1.6" Digital Grid Overlays, providing oversized miniature models (like alien Crushers or heavy cavalry) with appropriate physical clearance on your custom boards.
